name: Carson v. Makin
summary: The Supreme Court struck down Maine's exclusion of religious schools from its tuition assistance program, ruling that the distinction between status-based and use-based exclusions does not save a law that burdens religious exercise.
significance: Extended Espinoza to hold that states cannot exclude religious schools from tuition assistance programs because of the religious content of their instruction, which petitioners argue covers exclusions based on religious conduct as well as status.
